The camp's medical stores are running low, and the medic needs clean empty glass bottles to mix another batch of healing potions. They do not need to be rare, but they must be intact, sealable, and preferably not coated with swamp water or ruin dust. Once you bring them back, the medic can wash them, sterilize them, and split the new potions between the night patrol and the next scavenging team.
quest.echoes_of_survival.clear_raiders.d: A small raider crew has been circling the edge of the camp for several nights. They wait until the light drops, steal anything left outside the barricades, and try to pull isolated survivors into the ruined buildings nearby. Track their route, remove the threat, and return once the area is clear enough for the camp to send people outside again.
echoes_of_survival.quest.mechanic_iron_r: The camp is running out of usable metal parts, and the mechanic has already started stripping hinges, boiler plates, and broken tools just to keep the generator alive. A stack of standard iron ingots would let them brace the water pump, repair fence joints, and rebuild the stressed parts of the tools everyone keeps borrowing.

Bring enough iron back and the mechanic will put the most fragile camp equipment first, then pull a useful spare tool from the crate under the workbench for you. It is not glamorous work, but that metal may decide whether the barricade holds the next time a crowd gathers outside.
echoes_of_survival.quest.mechanic_torch_: Several lights along the north approach have gone out, leaving patrols to find their way with half-burned sticks and memory. The mechanic wants coal for a new batch of torches that can be placed along the fence, outside the storage shed, and near the medical tent. Once the coal arrives, those dark gaps can be lit before something uses them to slip into camp.
echoes_of_survival.quest.scavenger_salva: Rotten flesh scattered around the camp is drawing infected stragglers and hungry wildlife toward the safer paths. The scavenger wants it collected before the smell gets worse. It can still be used as bait, trap filler, or rough trade material, but leaving it on the roadside only makes every patrol less predictable.

The scavenger is willing to trade a portion of stored food for the rotten flesh you recover. It is unpleasant work, but it clears the patrol route and gives the camp a better idea of how many infected have been passing through. Wrap it well if you can; nobody wants that smell drifting through the sleeping area.
echoes_of_survival.quest.scavenger_zombi: A few zombies have started circling the camp perimeter, hiding behind trees and wrecked carts during the day before drifting toward voices and firelight after sunset. The scavenger is worried they will pull a larger group behind them. Clear the nearby infected, make sure they stay down, and report back before the next patrol walks into them.
